question: What is the primary definition of an infection reservoir?

options.A: The tool used to sterilize hospital equipment
options.B: The specific symptom caused by a parasite
options.C: A chemical substance that kills bacteria instantly
options.D: A place where pathogens live and multiply

explanation: A reservoir serves as the natural habitat where an infectious agent lives, grows, and multiplies. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is targeting the reservoir an effective strategy in disease control?

options.A: It permanently alters the genetic code of the virus
options.B: It eliminates the need for any handwashing protocols
options.C: It guarantees that patients develop lifelong immunity
options.D: It stops the infection cycle at its starting point

explanation: Intervening at the reservoir level prevents pathogens from surviving and spreading to new hosts. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h1)

question: Soil and water contaminated with pathogens are examples of which type of reservoir?
explanation: Non-living elements like soil, water, and food act as environmental reservoirs for various pathogens. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h2)

question: A healthy individual who carries a pathogen without showing symptoms belongs to which reservoir group?
explanation: Humans, including asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients, serve as human reservoirs for many communicable diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of isolating a patient with a communicable disease?

options.A: To prevent the spread of pathogens to healthy persons
options.B: To accelerate the natural mutation rate of the virus
options.C: To eliminate the need for administering medications
options.D: To ensure the patient receives a specialized diet

explanation: Isolation physically separates infected human reservoirs from susceptible individuals to halt transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is contact tracing considered essential when managing human reservoirs?

options.A: It helps identify asymptomatic or hidden cases quickly
options.B: It guarantees that patients will not experience side effects
options.C: It replaces the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: It provides financial compensation to infected families

explanation: Contact tracing uncovers secondary human reservoirs who may be spreading the disease without realizing it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h3)

question: What term describes infectious diseases that naturally transmit between animals and humans?
explanation: Zoonotic diseases originate in animal reservoirs and have the capacity to infect human populations. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h4)

question: A community nurse distributes insecticide-treated nets to prevent malaria. What is the main goal of this intervention?

options.A: To control the vector that transmits the disease
options.B: To sterilize the environmental soil and water supply
options.C: To isolate human reservoirs in a hospital ward
options.D: To treat individuals who already have chronic infections

explanation: Insecticide-treated nets target mosquito vectors, interrupting the transmission route from the reservoir to humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which intervention is most effective for managing waterborne environmental reservoirs?

options.A: Mass vaccination of local domestic livestock
options.B: Isolating infected human patients in private rooms
options.C: Administering antibiotics to healthy community members
options.D: Water chlorination and proper sewage disposal

explanation: Sanitation measures like water treatment and safe waste disposal destroy pathogens thriving in environmental water sources. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h5)

question: How do environmental reservoirs differ primarily from human reservoirs?

options.A: They consist of non-living habitats like soil and water
options.B: They only transmit viral infections through direct touch
options.C: They cannot be altered by public health interventions
options.D: They require active medical treatment to clear pathogens

explanation: Environmental reservoirs are inanimate substances and elements where pathogens survive independently of a host body. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h5)

question: What does disease eradication mean in public health terminology?

options.A: Treating all active human cases with oral drugs
options.B: Permanent reduction of worldwide infection to zero
options.C: Controlling insect vectors in a specific community
options.D: Lowering disease rates within a single local state

explanation: Eradication means the global elimination of a pathogen so that it no longer exists anywhere in nature. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does regional disease elimination differ from global eradication?

options.A: Elimination relies only on vector control, while eradication uses vaccines
options.B: Elimination is temporary, whereas eradication is only semi-permanent
options.C: Elimination targets a specific geographical area, while eradication is worldwide
options.D: Elimination applies strictly to animal reservoirs rather than humans

explanation: Elimination reduces cases to zero in a specific region or country, whereas eradication achieves this globally. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of disease surveillance in community nursing?

options.A: To collect and analyze health data to spot outbreaks early
options.B: To diagnose complex surgical conditions in hospitals
options.C: To manufacture vaccines in local community clinics
options.D: To provide financial grants to families affected by illness

explanation: Surveillance tracks disease patterns so nurses and health teams can detect and respond to outbreaks quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h7)

question: A community nurse notices a sudden rise in cholera cases. What immediate action should be taken?

options.A: Isolate the entire regional population in their homes
options.B: Report the findings and investigate the local water source
options.C: Advise residents to stop drinking all liquids entirely
options.D: Wait for patients to seek care without taking action

explanation: Investigating the environmental water source helps identify and neutralize the reservoir driving the outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h7)
